newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEEGAN RESIGNS AS NEWCASTLE'S MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEEGAN RESIGNS AS NEWCASTLE'S MANAGER.

text.p: Kevin Keegan resigned as manager of English premier league Newcastle United on Wednesday after nearly five years with the club, the Press Association reported.

Keegan, who will be 46 next month, reportedly told the Newcastle board he wanted to resign at the end of the season but both parties agreed it would be better if he left immediately. Keegan said he no longer wished to remain in football management at this stage of his life.

Keegan took over at Newcastle in February 1992 when they were facing relegation to the old third division of the English League but threatened to resign soon after joining the club when money he had been promised to strengthen the side was not made available.
But Newcastle's wealthy owner Sir John Hall persuaded him to stay and in the last five years they have rebuilt the team.

This time last year Newcastle led the premier league by 12 points and looked set for their first title since 1927 but the pressure told on Keegan and his side and they eventually finished four points behind Manchester United.

Newcastle have not been quite so consistent this season but are still in the title hunt and in their last two league matches have beaten Spurs 7-1 and Leeds 3-0. They drew 1-1 in the third round of the F.A. Cup at first division Charlton on Sunday.
